title: Exact exchange for derived cokernel adjunctions
statement: Let A,B,A',B' be abelian categories with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and n a natural number. Let E⊣R and E'⊣R' be additive adjunctions; R and R' are exact and R' is fully faithful. Suppose each ordinary unit X→REX (and X'→R'E'X') is the cokernel of n times the identity. Let L⊣D(R), L'⊣D(R') be shift-compatible derived adjunctions, with natural comparison morphisms ε:Q L→E_complex Q and ε' of the same kind. Suppose classes H,H' of complexes admit resolutions of every complex by quasi-isomorphisms, multiplication by n is monic in every term of each resolving complex, ε and ε' are invertible there, and the derived units there agree with the termwise ordinary units via ε and the exact-functor factorization. For exact additive F:A→A', G:B→B' and ρ:R F≅G R', there are isomorphisms e:E G≅F E' and θ:L D(G)≅D(F) L', normalized by the ordinary and derived mate-unit equations. θ commutes with shifts. On every complex P, θ followed by the target universal comparison equals the source universal comparison followed by the complex map induced by e, with the canonical exact-functor factorizations inserted.

proof.text: Exactness of F preserves the cokernel of n. The ordinary mate is the unique map of the two cokernel units; comparing their universal properties proves it invertible and fixes its unit equation.

Extend the two normalized unit equations from resolving complexes along resolution quasi-isomorphisms, using naturality of the unit, ε and the exact-functor factorization. Cancel the isomorphisms induced by the resolutions.

For any complex with termwise monic n, the unit is a degreewise cokernel, hence the multiplication sequence is short exact. A resolving quasi-isomorphism gives a map of multiplication short exact sequences. Its first two components are quasi-isomorphisms, so its third is too. Exact faithful R' reflects quasi-isomorphisms via homology, so ε' computes on this complex. F preserves monicity of n and therefore ε' computes on F of every source resolving complex.

Take the adjunction mate of D(ρ). Apply the target adjunction to its comparison with ε, and use the normalized units and ordinary mate equation. This proves the representative formula; on resolving complexes both ε comparisons are invertible, hence the mate is invertible. Extend by resolution and essential surjectivity of Q. Its inverse is θ. Units, counits, D(ρ), and thus the mate and its inverse commute with shifts.

theorem CategoryTheory.derivedCokernelAdjointExchange :
    ∃ e : E ⋙ G ≅ F ⋙ E',
      (∀ X, F.map (a.unit.app X) ≫ ρ.hom.app (E.obj X) ≫
        R'.map (e.hom.app X) = a'.unit.app (F.obj X)) ∧
      ∃ θ : L ⋙ G.mapDerivedCategory ≅ F.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ L',
        NatTrans.CommShift θ.hom ℤ ∧
        (∀ X, ad'.unit.app (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj X) ≫
          R'.mapDerivedCategory.map (θ.inv.app X) =
          F.mapDerivedCategory.map (ad.unit.app X) ≫
            (CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso ρ).hom.app (L.obj X)) ∧
        ∀ P : CochainComplex A ℤ,
          θ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
            L'.map (F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P) ≫
            ε'.app ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
          G.mapDerivedCategory.map (ε.app P) ≫
            G.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex e (.up ℤ)).hom.app P)
